title: TabICL: A Tabular Foundation Model for In-Context Learning on Large Data (ICML 2025) — Official Implementation
why_relevant: Directly matches the competition’s strongest public baseline family (TabICL) and documents practical knobs (n_estimators, outlier_threshold, checkpoint_version) plus auto-download behavior needed for a reproducible Kaggle/local kernel pipeline.
extracted_technique: Use TabICLClassifier with small n_estimators (16–64), quantile/none norms, outlier clipping, AMP on CUDA; ensemble by feature shuffling; reduce fold count if overfitting on small data; cache checkpoint locally to avoid repeated downloads.
takeaway: TabICL is a strong, GPU-friendly tabular foundation model with documented hyperparameters and checkpoint versioning; it supports automatic checkpoint download and can be run as a cheap fit + heavier predict, making it suitable for repeated CV + ensembling.

title: Implemented metrics | CatBoost
why_relevant: Confirms how to set and monitor AUC/Logloss in CatBoost and how best-iteration selection works, enabling a strong GPU-accelerated tree baseline that complements TabICL on small tabular data.
extracted_technique: Train CatBoostClassifier with eval_metric='AUC', early stopping (od_type/od_wait), use_best_model=True, GPU task_type; blend OOF predictions for ensemble.
query: CatBoost eval_metric AUC documentation loss_function Logloss
takeaway: CatBoost supports AUC as an evaluation metric and provides standard best-iteration/overfitting controls; it is a robust baseline/ensemble component for small tabular classification under AUC.

title: Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model | Nature
why_relevant: Establishes TabPFN as a high-performing foundation model for small tabular datasets (similar regime to 1.4k rows), motivating an optional zero/low-tuning candidate model if packaging/weights are feasible in the kernel environment.
extracted_technique: Apply a pretrained tabular foundation model for fast, strong small-data performance; consider as an additional ensemble member but guard behind dependency/weights availability checks.
query: TabPFN Nature tabular foundation model PriorLabs
takeaway: TabPFN-style foundation models can outperform heavily tuned baselines on small tabular tasks with minimal training; in competitions, they are best used as a guarded optional component or ensemble member due to environment constraints.

title: TabPFN-2.5: Advancing the State of the Art in Tabular Foundation Models (arXiv:2511.08667)
why_relevant: Provides the most concrete, citable technical reference for TabPFN-2.5 capabilities and scaling claims, useful for deciding whether to invest in integrating a foundation model versus sticking to GBDT + TabICL ensemble.
extracted_technique: If weights are accessible, use a modern tabular foundation model as an additional predictor; otherwise fall back to GBDTs + TabICL; avoid any method that requires private credentials or non-reasonable access.
takeaway: TabPFN-2.5 reports strong performance on tabular benchmarks and can be a powerful optional model, but practical integration should be guarded to avoid brittle downloads/licensing issues in Kaggle/runtime environments.
